next.name: Silent Librarian
next.headline: Silent Librarian: a group that phishes universities at the start of each academic year
next.in_short: Malwarebytes describes Silent Librarian as an APT that runs spear phishing against universities with fake login and library pages. It has done so around each new academic year since 2018.

sentences.t: Malwarebytes' Threat Intelligence Team reports on a threat actor known as Silent Librarian, also tracked as TA407 and COBALT DICKENS.
In March 2018, the US Department of Justice indicted nine Iranians for attacks on universities and other organisations, according to the report.
The report says it has gone after the same kind of victims in over a dozen countries.
The group runs spear phishing campaigns, using phishing sites that imitate university login and library pages.
Malwarebytes says the actor uses Cloudflare for most of its phishing hostnames to hide the real hosting origin.

Malwarebytes says it found some of the group's infrastructure on Iran-based hosting. It notes it may seem odd for an attacker to use infrastructure in their own country, since that could point a finger at them.
Malwarebytes says registering subdomains for phishing against universities is known behaviour for this APT, so it expects the same actor registered them.
According to the report, the group has targeted universities around each new academic year since 2018, and was lining up for the new academic year in both August 2018 and 2019.
In mid-September, a customer tipped Malwarebytes off about a new active campaign from the group. The report was published on 2020-10-14.
Malwarebytes says it uncovered only a small portion of this phishing operation.
University staff and students should treat login and library pages reached through emailed links with caution, especially at the start of term.
